title: Scanning a paired bit string
statement: Let $x,w$ be finite bit strings, let $b$ be either true or false, and let $v$ assign a natural-number counter to each of the program’s 13 registers. Suppose every counter is at most $4(|x|+1)$, register $1$ equals register $0$ plus $|w|$, and for every $j<|w|$ the bit of $x$ at position $v(0)+j$ (taken to be false when out of range) equals the bit of $w$ at position $j$ (also taken to be false when out of range). If the paired-string parser fails on $w$, the program can reach its false-answer state after advancing register $0$ by some $t\le |w|$, while maintaining its safety conditions at every earlier step. If the parser returns $(a,\_)$, it can reach the copy state indexed by $b$ after advancing register $0$ by $2|a|+2$, again maintaining those conditions at every earlier step.
hypotheses_covered: The stated position-by-position agreement between $x$ and $w$
